tasks.title: Doubling time — discrete annual growth
tasks.context: A quantity grows by the discrete annual factor $1.03$ each year, so $f(t)=f_0\cdot(1.03)^{t}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The exact doubling time is strictly less than $25$ years.
The rule-of-$72$ estimate $0.72/r$ lies within $0.5$ years of the exact doubling time.
Over a $10$-year window the accumulation factor exceeds $1.5$.
The doubling time equals $1/r$ with $r=0.03$.
The exact doubling time exceeds $24$ years.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$t\approx23.4498$$

$$23.4498 < 25$$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$|0.72/r - t|\approx0.5502$$ compared with $0.5$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$(1.03)^{10}\approx1.343916$$

$$1.343916 ≤ 1.5$$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Linearised $1/r=33.3333$ vs exact $23.4498$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$23.4498 ≤ 24$$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Discrete annual growth $f(t)=f_0\cdot(1.03)^{t}$. Doubling:

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{\ln(1.03)}\approx23.4498$$

Rule-of-$72$ estimate $\approx24.0000$.

tasks.title: Sorn — continuous population force
tasks.context: A regional demographer models the population of Sorn by $f(t)=6\,e^{0.04t}$, where $t$ is years after a census and $f(t)$ is measured in millions of residents. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The doubling time of $f$ is strictly less than $15$ years.
At $t=7$, the population exceeds $9$ million.
The continuous annual growth rate encoded by the model is exactly $4\%$.
The same path is given by the discrete annual model $f(t)=6\,(1+0.04)^{t}$.
Because the exponent is $0.04t$, the population increases by exactly $4\%$ of its previous year-end value each calendar year.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Doubling means $f(t)=2f(0)$, so

$$e^{0.04t}=2$$

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.04}$$

$$t\approx17.3287$$

Compare with $15$:

$$17.3287>15$$.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Substitute $t=7$:

$$f(7)=6\,e^{0.04\cdot7}$$

$$\approx7.9388$$

Compare with $9$ million:

$$7.9388 ≤ 9$$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

In $f(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$ the continuous annual force is the coefficient $k$.

$$k=0.04$$

$$100k=4$$

The claim asserts exactly $4\%$, which matches $100k$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

A discrete annual model with nominal rate $r=0.04$ is

$$g(t)=6\,(1+0.04)^{t}$$

Continuous compounding uses $e^{kt}$. These agree for all $t$ only if $1+r=e^{k}$.

$$1+0.04=1.04$$

$$e^{0.04}\approx1.040811$$

Since $1.04\neq e^{0.04}$, the paths differ.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Under continuous force $k$, the one-year multiplier is $e^{k}$, not $1+k$.

$$e^{0.04}-1\approx0.040811$$

$$100(e^{k}-1)\approx4.0811\%$$

That is not exactly $4\%$ in the discrete year-over-year sense.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
The overview recovers the continuous model

$$f(t)=6\,e^{0.04t}$$

with $t$ in years and $f$ in millions of people in Sorn. The continuous annual force is $k=0.04$, so $100k=4\%$. Doubling solves $e^{kt}=2$, hence $t=\ln 2/k\approx17.3287$. At $t=7$, $f(7)\approx7.9388$ million.

tasks.title: Radioactive sample — half-life 6 h
tasks.context: A lab sample of mass $m_0=64$ grams decays with half-life $T_{1/2}=6$ hours under $m(t)=m_0 e^{-kt}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.

tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\frac{18}{6}=3$$

$$8 ≤ 10$$.

So the statement is False.

Solve $m(t)=10$:

$$64\,e^{-kt}=10$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(64/10)}{k}\approx16.0684$$

$$16.0684 < 18$$.

So the statement is True.

$$k=\frac{\ln 2}{6}\approx0.115525$$

and

At $t=18$, $m(18)=8$.

$$\frac{18}{6}=3$$

From the overview, $m(18)=8$.

$$8 ≤ 10$$

The rewritten claim denies that failed comparison, so it holds.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Solve $m(t)=10$:

$$64\,e^{-kt}=10$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(64/10)}{k}\approx16.0684$$

$$16.0684 < 18$$.

So the statement is True.

tasks.title: Sorn — continuous population force

**A.** → False

Doubling means $f(t)=2f(0)$, so

$$e^{0.04t}=2$$

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.04}$$

$$17.3287>15$$.

**B.** → False

Substitute $t=7$:

$$f(7)=6\,e^{0.04\cdot7}$$

$$\approx7.9388$$

Compare with $9$ million:

So the statement is False.

In $f(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$ the continuous annual force is the coefficient $k$.

$$k=0.04$$

$$100k=4$$

So the statement is True.

A discrete annual model with nominal rate $r=0.04$ is

$$g(t)=6\,(1+0.04)^{t}$$

Continuous compounding uses $e^{kt}$. These agree for all $t$ only if $1+r=e^{k}$.

$$1+0.04=1.04$$

$$e^{0.04}\approx1.040811$$

Since $1.04\neq e^{0.04}$, the paths differ.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Under continuous force $k$, the one-year multiplier is $e^{k}$, not $1+k$.

$$e^{0.04}-1\approx0.040811$$
